entries.tactical_failure_mode_quoted: The signature failure is treating the reframing as a mechanical wrapper: taking an established attribution, decomposition, or estimation tool and pointing it at a new input granularity, a new architecture, or a new domain without re-deriving why the resulting scores are faithful to the model. These papers supply the computation but not the justification — no causal validation that the identified components actually drive behavior (only correlation), no axiomatic or soundness argument for why the proposed definition is the 'real' importance, and no confound control, so a reviewer can point to a methodological artifact (a computation-granularity difference, a degenerate zero baseline, an off-manifold perturbation) that explains the result instead.

entries.tactical_pattern_quoted: This cluster recasts an opaque transparency question about an already-trained model or dataset — which feature/datum/internal component is responsible, how uncertain a prediction is, what a hidden representation encodes — as a concrete measurement over a well-studied object: a manifold-constrained counterfactual optimization, a submodular subset selection, an expectation/estimator over marginal statistics, an additive decomposition into a (often sparse) basis, or an influence/Shapley score accumulated along the optimization trajectory. The decisive move is choosing the right unit of analysis and the right faithfulness constraint so the resulting scores reflect the model's actual computation rather than an off-distribution or post-hoc artifact — e.g., searching counterfactuals only on the learned data manifold, decomposing into monosemantic sparse directions before causal tracing, or embedding the explanatory predictors as the primary decision representation.
